protocol.name: qdwin_locker_v1
protocol.description:
Private protocol between the qdwin compositor and the qdistro PyQt locker (qdlocker). Same trust model as qdwin_shell_v1: qdwin only advertises this global to clients whose peer credentials (uid, exe, SELinux label) match the admin-configured locker identity. Regular app clients never see it; the shell client (qdwin_shell_v1) does not see it either — the locker is a separate peer process from the shell.
Why a separate global from qdwin_shell_v1:
- The shell client and the locker client have different lifetimes. The shell can crash and restart while the locker is live; the locker can crash and restart while the shell is composing decorations. Wiring them through a single global would couple their lifecycles. - attach_lock_surface needs a wl_surface from the same wl_display that bound the global. Forcing the shell to attach the locker's surface would require a cross-process wl_surface handoff, which Wayland does not provide. - The locker is the only process allowed to drive the compositor's `locked` state. Keeping that authority on its own global lets qdwin filter it independently from the shell's chrome / focus requests.
The compositor remains authoritative over lock state. The locker requests `set_locked(1)`, but qdwin is the actor: it hides all non-lock surfaces, mutes input to them, and emits `locked_changed`. The shell observes via the existing qdwin_shell_v1 `locked_changed` event and swaps its UI off.
Warning! Experimental and pre-stable. Versioning follows the "experimental" convention: version 1 is the first unstable draft.

interface.name: qdwin_locker_v1
interface.description:
The locker binds this global once and holds it for the lifetime of its process. qdwin rejects a second bind from the same client. If a new locker comes up while the old one is still bound, qdwin destroys the old binding (the old process is considered dead — only one locker may exist at a time).
Bootstrap: until the locker has sent `bind_as_locker` and attached a lock surface, qdwin treats `set_locked` requests as no-ops. The compositor starts in locked state by default (see sessions.md §"Admin logout / compositor crash") and waits for the locker to attach its surface before showing anything.
If the locker process dies while the compositor is in locked state, qdwin keeps the screen black and refuses input until a replacement locker binds. Admin's compositor is the trusted computing base; a missing locker is fail-safe (locked), not fail-open.

entry.name: already_bound
entry.summary: locker is already bound by another process

request.name: bind_as_locker
request.description: The locker announces that it is ready to receive lock-trigger events and to drive lock state. Must be the first request on the interface. qdwin replies with `ready` once it has confirmed the peer credentials and registered the binding.

event.name: ready
event.description: Sent after `bind_as_locker` succeeds. The locker should now attach its lock surface and (if the compositor is already locked) wait for the user to authenticate.

arg.name: initially_locked
arg.summary: 1 if the compositor is currently locked, 0 otherwise

request.name: attach_lock_surface
request.description:
Places `surface` on the compositor LOCK layer, covering every output. The surface is not yet "live" — the lock state is still driven by `set_locked`. Multiple lock surfaces are not allowed; a second attach replaces the first and dismisses the prior surface.
The surface must not have a role yet. After attach, it has the implicit "lock surface" role; any wl_surface.commit triggers a frame on the LOCK layer.

request.name: set_locked
request.description:
`locked=1` → compositor enters the locked state: the lock surface (from attach_lock_surface) is the only thing composited; user-session surfaces stop rendering; input is delivered only to the locker via `overlay_key`.
`locked=0` → unlocks; user surfaces resume rendering. The locker is expected to call this only after a successful authentication.
Compositor emits `locked_changed(locked)` to the shell on qdwin_shell_v1 after the transition completes, and emits the equivalent `locked_changed` event on this interface to the locker.
Fails with `no_surface` if no lock surface is attached.

event.name: locked_changed

description.summary: compositor entered or left locked state

event.description: Mirror of qdwin_shell_v1.locked_changed for the locker. Fires on every transition, including transitions the locker did not request (e.g. the lid-close path inside the compositor).

event.name: lock_requested

description.summary: user pressed the manual-lock keybinding or lid closed

event.description:
Aggregates the triggers in sessions.md §"Lock triggers" that the compositor observes directly:
reason = 0 idle — ext-idle-notify-v1 timeout reason = 1 lid — systemd-logind lid close reason = 2 suspend — prepare-for-sleep reason = 3 manual — Ctrl+Alt+L global hotkey or admin panel "Lock now"
The locker decides whether to call `set_locked(1)` (it usually does immediately, but may delay if a fingerprint verification is already in progress).

event.name: overlay_key
event.description:
While the lock surface is attached and the compositor is locked, qdwin installs a keyboard grab and forwards each pressed key to the locker here. Identical wire format to qdwin_shell_v1.overlay_key (since v17) for the role=2 (locker) value, but delivered on the locker's connection so the shell cannot observe lock-time keystrokes — i.e. the password the user types never reaches the shell process.
`sym` is the xkb keysym; `utf8` is the printable character (or "" if non-printable). The locker prefers utf8 when non-empty and falls back to `sym` for control keys (Escape, Return, BackSpace, Tab).
Only PRESSED transitions are sent. Releases are absorbed by the grab.

request.name: lock_acknowledged
request.description: Tells the compositor the locker has handled (or deliberately ignored) a `lock_requested` event. Used for tests and for deciding whether the compositor should escalate (e.g. drop to a black screen if the locker fails to lock within a reasonable window after suspend).

arg.name: reason
arg.summary: must match the most recent lock_requested.reason

interface.name: qdwin_locker_surface_v1

description.summary: handle to a previously-attached lock surface

interface.description: Created by `qdwin_locker_v1.attach_lock_surface`. Destroying this object dismisses the lock surface; if the compositor is currently locked, the screen goes black until a fresh attach_lock_surface fires.

event.name: configure
event.description: Tells the locker the dimensions it should commit a buffer at to cover every output. Re-fires on output hot-plug or rotation.
